newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates up, dollar/Germany cited.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates up, dollar/Germany cited.

text.p: Dutch money market rates across the board climbed further on Tuesday as the guilder continued to weaken against the dollar and as equivalent German rates rose.
Call money was bid at 3.18 percent -- unchanged from Monday -- but dealers said it changed hands at 3.25 and 3.31 percent.
Deposits up to one year also traded two or three basis points higher than on Monday, compensating for the weakening guilder against the dollar, dealers said.
One month-deposits were set at 3.26/34 percent bid/ask, up from 3.24/32 on Monday, while one year-deposits climbed to 3.58/66 percent bid/ask from 3.56/64.
"With the dollar getting stronger and stronger, (Dutch money market) rates had to be adjusted," one dealer said.
At 0930 GMT, the dollar stood at 2.1150/56 guilders bid/ask, firmed from 2.1068 on Monday afternoon.
German money market rates were also slightly higher.
In line with market developments, the Finance Ministry's Agency slightly raised indicative prices for Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) this morning, dealers said.
DTCs maturing this month were set at 3.25 percent, September paper at 3.27 percent, and October DTCs at 3.30 percent.
The indicative prices for DTCs maturing in December and June were raised to 3.31 and 3.52 percent respectively.
Dealers did not expect the central bank to raise its special advances rate when it announces a new pact on Thursday, but they added fears had not totally faded among market players.
"Looking at the guilder/mark, I don't see a reason (to hike the rate) at the moment," one said.
The guilder was changing hands at 112.6350 per 100 marks, below its ERM central rate of 112.673.
